<RecipePage recipeId="batch-retrieve-documents">

<RecipeSection label="Problem">

You already have a mix of document IDs and URLs, and you want the indexed documents you can open without one request per document. One experimental batch accepts 1 to 100 document IDs or URLs. It prints the documents Glean returns under results, and the document IDs or URLs it does not return under warnings. The published TypeScript API client does not include these endpoints, so this example calls the HTTP API and uses the official auth package for sign-in.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeCodeWalkthrough />

<RecipeArchitecture />

<RecipePrereqs />

<RecipeSteps />

<RecipeSection label="Keep the experimental header on every request">

This client sets X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. Keep that header if you add a call. A 404 with the header usually means your Glean instance has not turned these endpoints on. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Request only documents:read">

OAuth login and the token provider use the documents:read scope. Do not add other scopes. If you create an API token instead, choose Read documents (documents:read). On the legacy token screen, choose DOCUMENTS.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Treat warnings as a successful batch">

HTTP 200 with warnings means Glean finished the batch and did not return some document IDs or URLs. You see Retrieved N of M documents, then results and warnings, and the command exits 0. Exit non-zero only when the request itself fails, including HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, and 413.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Experimental endpoints">

These endpoints are experimental and can change. This client sends X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. If your Glean instance has not turned the endpoints on, you still get HTTP 404. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support. The published @gleanwork/api-client package has no methods for these endpoints. client.documents reads documents through a different API. Do not call it here.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Some documents cannot be retrieved">

A Gmail or Outlook search result or chat citation can show an ID that only works in that result. Do not pass that ID to --id. Pass the message URL with --url. That URL can still appear under warnings with code resource_not_found. Go links and federated search results cannot be retrieved. You only get documents you can open.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="A missing document is a warning, not its own status">

Each document ID or URL appears under results or under warnings. The warning shows a code and Glean's message. resource_not_found and invalid_parameter are examples of codes Glean may return. Glean can return other codes. There is no separate status field on each document. An empty or malformed URL is listed under warnings on HTTP 200. It is not HTTP 400. This CLI rejects a blank --url or --id before it sends the request, so you see an error that names the flag. HTTP 413 means the request body is too large. Sending more than 100 document IDs and URLs is rejected in this CLI before the request, and that error is not HTTP 413.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Content is extracted text, not the file">

include CONTENT adds content.full_text_list on every document Glean returns. An empty list means Glean stored no extracted text. You still see the document, with content_segments: 0. If Glean cannot read the text you asked for, the command fails instead of printing documents without content. The command prints the segment count, not every segment.

</RecipeSection>

<TakeItFurther>

- Pass --content when you need extracted text. Each result line includes content_segments: N. content_segments: 0 means Glean stored no extracted text. You still see the document. If Glean cannot read the text you asked for, the command fails.
- Copy the document ID in parentheses on the results line and pass it to --id. You can also copy the document_id line from retrieve-document-by-url.
- For a Gmail or Outlook message, pass the message URL with --url, not the ID from the search result or chat citation.

</TakeItFurther>
